overview.title: Thuya, Silver and Argan Under the Lanes
overview.p1: Essaouira’s craft identity is tactile: thuya-wood marquetry with its sharp resin scent, silver jewellery lighter than imperial-city pieces, and argan oil from cooperatives with clearer labelling.
overview.p2: Many workshops open onto the street so you can watch the lathe or the bench. Quality varies — for wood, check the finish; for argan, prefer cooperative brands.
overview.p3: Keep shopping as one loop in a day that also includes the Skala and a port lunch, so the visit does not collapse into transactions only.

q1.question: Is bargaining expected?
q1.answer: Yes in many stalls; some cooperatives use fixed prices.

q2.question: Can I photograph craftsmen?
q2.answer: Ask first — most accept a polite request.

q3.question: Can I ship wood abroad?
q3.answer: Rules vary; confirm with the seller before paying.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Artisan Souks?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for history and local context.

q5.question: Is Artisan Souks suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes with normal supervision near busy lanes or workshops.
